source.title: Billion-Scale Graph Foundation Models
source.authors: Maya Bechler-Speicher; Yoel Gottlieb; A. Isakov; David Abensur; A. Tavory; Daniel Haimovich; Ido Guy; Udi Weinsberg

record.file_problem: The supplied text is a full paper; no relevant truncation or garbling is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how model size relates to held-out loss in billion-scale heterogeneous graph models, a new domain and setting for the mapped claim. It does not test memorization of random labels or most of the claim's intervention conditions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a model-size scaling sweep with validation loss on a held-out graph component. This bears on V2's model-size dimension, but does not test widening past the zero-training-error threshold in the specified ReLU setup. Other architecture ablations compare downstream task performance, not training-to-test generalization gaps. Reported results on downstream graphs are out-of-distribution and do not establish same-distribution generalization.
record.test_reason: The study measures graph-model scaling and transfer performance, but tests none of V1–V8. Its parameter-count sweep reports best validation loss without identifying a width intervention or establishing zero training error, so it cannot test V2's improvement beyond the interpolation threshold. Batch-size motivation cites Keskar et al., but no batch-size comparison is reported.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the scaling conclusion and its Enterprise-dataset limitation. It omits the authors' broader conclusion that billion-scale GraphBFF learns transferable representations: frozen-model probing achieves the best reported performance across ten unseen downstream task graphs, including few-shot evaluations.
record.recipe_differences: Billion-scale graph foundation-model pretraining on real-world heterogeneous graph data with masked link prediction; it does not use the mapped claim's natural-label image-classification or random-label memorization procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: Held-out loss varies with model size and training-data size; the authors report bottlenecks and saturation when one is fixed. Downstream performance also varies with task and context size.

fits_no_version.finding: Across nine model sizes and eight training-data sizes, GraphBFF validation loss decreases with either resource until the other becomes limiting. The study uses early-stopped validation loss on approximately six million held-out edges and does not locate an interpolation threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For GraphBFF masked-link prediction on the Enterprise graph, held-out loss follows model- and data-size scaling trends, with diminishing returns when either resource is fixed.

fits_no_version.finding: Frozen pretrained GraphBFF representations with trained probes outperform the tested task-specific baselines when selecting the best context for each of ten downstream tasks; TCA-only and TAA-only ablations perform worse than the full pretrained model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GraphBFF pretraining produces transferable representations for unseen Enterprise task graphs, and combining its two attention components improves downstream performance.

record.problems: The scaling results are limited to one Enterprise dataset and may not transfer to graphs with different degree distributions or feature spaces. The paper reports held-out loss curves but no training-to-test error gap or memorization-capacity check.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained. The model-size sweep reports validation/held-out loss but not the training error needed to establish the V2 interpolation-threshold claim; its specific models and setting also differ from V2. Other tables concern downstream-task performance or architectural ablations, not training-to-test gaps.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, chance-level held-out performance on random labels, and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and training recipe.
Whether increasing width beyond that required for zero training error continues lowering test error; the interpolation threshold is not established.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contributions of local connectivity, learned sparsity, and convolutional initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers under limited or broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, and optimizer switching.
Large versus small batches under matched epoch budgets, including adaptations that reduce the penalty.

Controlled dropout comparisons, small-data effects, excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation. Searching over dropout configurations does not establish these effects.
Magnitude-aware sharpness as a predictor of generalization gaps and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy loss.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the reader's tests/T3 classification and V2 tested_not_extracted assignment. Parameter-count scaling alone does not establish post-interpolation width generalization. No version-relevant results require missing rows; the scaling and downstream results were already declared in rows_left_out. Generalization gaps are not required for every version, but the specific interventions and comparisons named by those versions are absent here.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence; all specified models, datasets and training recipes.

The model-size scaling sweep relates larger model size to held-out loss, but does not report matched training error, zero training error, or the specified one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10. No row directly tests whether widening past the interpolation threshold keeps lowering test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, local connectivity, learned sparse connections, and convolutional initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers, tuning regimes, weight decay, optimizer switching and language-model results.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measured properties as predictors of training-to-test generalization gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Appendix B discusses large-batch optimization concerns and cites Keskar et al. (2017), but does not compare held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets or use that finding as an experimental tool.

tranche.reason: No results test V1–V8. Section 6 measures validation-loss scaling with parameter count and data size, without establishing a width intervention or zero training error required for V2.

source_check.notes: The pack lists no rows, statements, or verdicts. The reported graph-transfer and scaling results concern generalization broadly but do not test the catalog's specified claim versions.
